title: protobase.config.json
description: A Protobase project's config, as protobase.config.ts's ProtobaseConfig types it: one flat object of plain data, everything optional.

$schema.description: The JSON Schema this file follows, such as ./node_modules/@protobase/config/schema.json.

themeColor.description: The colour of the installed app's title bar and of the browser's toolbar around it.

backgroundColor.description: The colour of the screen an installed app shows while it starts.

name.description: The app's name: sign-in prompts, the mail it sends, the tab titles and the installed app; `PROTOBASE_APP_NAME` overrides it. Default `Protobase`.

url.description:
The app's public URL, such as `https://admin.example.com`: the issuer of its tokens and where its emails link to.
Default `PROTOBASE_URL`, or in `protobase dev` the dev server's own; required with sign-in otherwise.

secret.description:
The app's secret, made with `openssl rand -base64 32`: it signs session cookies, upload tickets and download links
and public forms' bot checks, and encrypts the token signing keys. Default `PROTOBASE_SECRET`; required with sign-in.

previousSecrets.description:
The app's secrets before `secret`, newest first: what they encrypted still decrypts, so the token signing keys keep
signing after the secret changes. Keep one listed while the keys it encrypted sign (`signingKeyDays`), and while
two-factor authenticator apps set up with it are in use. Default `PROTOBASE_PREVIOUS_SECRETS`, comma separated.

signingKeyDays.description: Days a token signing key signs before a new one takes over. Default 30.

signingKeyGraceDays.description: Days a replaced signing key still verifies the tokens it signed. Default 7, at least 1.

locale.description: The language of the admin app's built-in screens and of its numbers and dates, for every user: `'en'` or `'nl'`; unset, each user's browser's.

timezone.description: The time zone the jobs' schedules are read in unless a job names its own, such as `Europe/Amsterdam`. Default `UTC`.

apiKeys.description:
The app's publishable and secret keys, with which supabase-js calls the PostgREST-compatible `/api/sb/rest/v1` and the
Realtime-compatible `/api/sb/realtime/v1` and the Storage-compatible `/api/sb/storage/v1` (see `ApiKeysOptions`); default `PROTOBASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` and
`PROTOBASE_SECRET_KEY`. Without either, or with `false`, the app serves neither.

statementTimeoutMs.description:
How long a query of an API request may run, set on every request's transaction with SET LOCAL; a query that runs
longer is a 504 that names the request. Default 1000: a query that needs longer wants an index or a simpler filter,
or belongs in a function or job with `longQueries`.

scanGuard.description: Reads that filter, sort or count values by a column no index serves. Default mode `reject`.

defaultAccess.description: What an operation without a rule does; overrides the capability check. Without `roles` the default is allow.

rowPermissions.description: Whether list items carry their `permissions` (update, delete): true by default, or `{ except: [...] }` for resources that opt out.

errorReporting.description:
Where the app's errors go: the server's 500s, stopped queries and crashes, and the admin app's errors in the
browser (see `ErrorReportingOptions`). Defaults to the DSN the platform passes in `PROTOBASE_SENTRY_DSN`; `false`
turns it off.

cors.description:
The websites whose browser code may call the API (`/api/*` but `/api/auth/*`) besides the app's own origins (see
`auth.origins`): a list of origins, or `*` for any. Defaults to the one the platform passes in
`PROTOBASE_CORS_ORIGINS` (`*` or comma separated), when set. A `mobile` section adds the app's Capacitor origins
(`capacitor://localhost`, `https://localhost`). With none of these nor other origins, the API sends no CORS headers.

maps.description:
The map style the app's maps (`l.map`, `d.map`) are drawn with, and the layers they may switch to (see
`MapOptions`). The style defaults to the one the platform passes in `PROTOBASE_MAP_STYLE_URL`; without either, or
with `false`, the app draws no maps.

plugins.description:
The plugins the admin app loads (see `PluginOption`), before the ones the platform lists in `PROTOBASE_PLUGINS`
and, for those that load before sign-in, `PROTOBASE_PLUGINS_BEFORE_SIGN_IN`; `false` turns all of them off.

apiPath.description: The path of the REST API; default `/api/v1` (`AdminOptions['basePath']`).

writeHooks.description: The write hooks by name, run in this order inside each write's transaction; each is `hooks/<name>.ts`.

mcpEndpoint.description:
The MCP endpoint's tools: `sql`, `writes`, or `false` for a host that serves its own (`AdminOptions['mcp']`);
`auth.mcp` turns MCP on. The app's own tools are mcp/tools.ts's.

runtimeUpdates.description: The runtime updates endpoint behind the top bar's update button (`AdminOptions['runtime']`).

remoteResources.description: Other Protobase APIs whose resources the admin app draws as its own (`AdminOptions['sources']`).

auth.description:
Sign-in (see `AuthConfig`), on by default with its own defaults; `false` turns it off, as does an
`authenticate.jwksUrl` that trusts an auth server elsewhere. Its hooks are `auth/hooks.ts`.

authenticate.description: How the API verifies tokens; default the tokens of `auth` (see `AuthenticateSettings`).

jobs.description: The app's jobs by name: what each does, its arguments and when it runs; its run is `jobs/<name>.ts`.

events.description: Where the changes that resources' events are raised from are captured (see `EventsOptions`).

history.description: How long the history of resources with `.history()` is kept (see `HistoryOptions`).

webhooks.description: Webhook subscriptions made in the admin app (see `WebhooksOptions`); `{}` turns them on.

schema.description: The schema of the subscriptions table and the deliveries view; default `webhooks`.

deliveryLog.description: Also keep every try, successes too, for 30 days, listed as Webhook delivery log. Default false.

allowPrivateAddresses.description:
Lets subscriptions send to private, loopback and link-local addresses, for development and tests. Default false:
a URL whose host resolves to one is refused, so a subscription cannot reach the app's own network.

realtime.description: How supabase-js's Realtime is served: `{ processes: 'many' }` when several processes serve the app (see `RealtimeOptions`).

notifications.description: Each user's devices and inbox (see `NotificationsOptions`); `{}` turns them on.

schema.description: The schema of the built-in tables; default `notifications`.

ui.description: The bell in the top bar; default true. `false` keeps only the backend.

devices.description: The devices table: its name, default `devices`, and its columns named otherwise than Protobase names them.

history.description: The history table: its name, default `history`, and its columns named otherwise than Protobase names them.

mobile.description: The app's iOS and Android build (see `MobileConfig`).

EnvValue.description: A value read from the environment variable `$env`: `default` when it is unset or empty, and with `split` the list of its non-empty parts.

roles.description:
The roles users can have, for example `['admin', 'accountant', 'warehouse']`. `admin` is always included; default
`['admin', 'user']`. With `organizations`, give each a label, and optionally the other roles its holders may also
give members: `{ manager: { label: 'Manager', grants: ['sales'] }, sales: 'Sales' }`.

mcp.description: Turns on the OAuth provider for MCP clients: `true`, or the endpoint's `path` and the `connectPage`.

path.description: The path of the MCP endpoint on the app's origin, its OAuth resource; default `/api/mcp`. Changing it makes clients connect again.

connectPage.description: The connect page's path on the app's origin, where people sign in and allow a client; default `/-/connect`, for a UI at the root.

generateUserId.description: `'uuid'` gives new users a random UUID, and makes every id column of the store a `uuid`; `generateUserId` in the hooks takes the ids from the app instead.

mailer.description: `false` turns mail off whatever the environment says; default SMTP from `PROTOBASE_SMTP_URL` and `PROTOBASE_MAIL_FROM`.

organizations.description: Turns on organizations (see `OrganizationsOptions`); their hooks are in the hooks module.

creatorAppRoles.description: The app roles an organization's creator holds there: `'all'` (default), every role a member can hold, or a list.

create.description: Who may create organizations: `'admins'` (default), superusers only, or `'everyone'` signed in.

invitationDays.description: How long an invitation works, in days. Default 7.

membershipLimit.description: The most members an organization can have. Default 1000.

deleteRecords.description:
What deleting an organization does with its records: `'refuse'` (default) deletes only an organization without
rows in any `.tenant` resource; `'cascade'` leaves it to the project's foreign keys.

invitationUrl.description: The page an invitation link opens, with `?token=`. Default `{baseURL}/-/invitation`.

origins.description:
The other origins the app is served on, for example `['https://admin.shop.com']`. A request to one of them is
answered for that host: its sign-in callbacks and the links it mails, such as a password reset, stay there, and
passkeys work on every origin. Tokens keep `baseURL` as issuer, whatever host issued them. Defaults to the
comma-separated list the platform passes in `PROTOBASE_ORIGINS`, when set; none otherwise.

passkeyDomain.description:
The host new passkeys are made for (their RP ID): the host of `baseURL` or of one of `origins`. Each passkey keeps
the one it was made for, and works on every origin, so changing it breaks none. Defaults to the one the platform
passes in `PROTOBASE_PASSKEY_DOMAIN`, when set, and to the host of `baseURL` otherwise.

trustedOrigins.description: Extra origins that may call the auth endpoints, such as the exact host of a dev tunnel. `baseURL` and `origins` are always trusted.

defaultRole.description:
The role of a user created without one. Optional: when unset, and more than one role besides `admin` exists,
creating a user without a role is an error that asks for one. With exactly one other role, that role is the default.

signUp.description:
Open sign-up: anyone makes their own account from the sign-in page, with `role`, after proving their address with
an emailed code. Off by default, so accounts come only from the host, an admin, an invitation or a sign-in provider.
Needs a mailer: without one it is not offered. `role` is one of `roles` and never `admin`; give it the least
a stranger may hold. Not with `organizations`, whose people come from invitations.

signInPolicy.description:
The sign-in policy that applies until an admin saves one on the Sign-in policy page, and when the saved one no
longer reads: the methods it names, for example `{ password: 'forbidden' }` for emailed codes and passkeys only,
with everything else allowed. Checked at startup as an admin's save is. Default everything allowed.

signInFirst.description:
What the sign-in page leads with: `password`, the email address and a password, with emailing a code below it; or
`emailCode`, the address and "Email me a sign-in code", with the password behind "Use a password", for apps whose
people mostly never set one. Only while the policy leaves both on; default `password`.

signInPerMinute.description: Sign-in attempts allowed per minute and client, default 5; also the sign-up requests allowed.

socialProviders.description:
Sign-in providers for Better Auth, for example `{ github: { clientId, clientSecret } }`; the callback is
`{baseURL}/api/auth/callback/<provider>`. A provider also signs up people without an account, with the default role.
One with the id of `signInProvider` takes its place. Default none.

encryptOAuthTokens.description: Encrypt the OAuth access, refresh and ID tokens Better Auth stores for social sign-ins, with `secret`. Default off.

users.description:
The user table, when it is one another system made, such as Supabase's `auth.users`: its name, the columns named
otherwise than Protobase names them, and a JSON column for each user's metadata, for example `{ table: 'users',
columns: { role: 'app_role' }, metadata: 'raw_user_meta_data' }`. The other tables keep their names. Default the
table `protobase auth migration` makes.

passwordHashes.description:
Password hashes another system wrote that sign-in accepts besides Better Auth's own, such as `['bcrypt']` for
Supabase Auth's. The first sign-in with one stores the password again as Better Auth hashes it. Default none.

leakedPasswords.description:
Refuses a new password that appears in a known data breach, by Have I Been Pwned's password list: at sign-up, from
an invitation, and when a password is set, changed, reset or given by an admin. Only the first five characters of
the password's SHA-1 hash leave the server. While the list cannot be reached, setting a password fails. Default off.

accountDeletion.description:
Lets the signed-in person delete their own account from the account page, with their password or from a session
that signed in within the last day; `false` turns it off, for apps whose accounts are managed by an organization's
admins. Default on, as app stores require an app that makes accounts to delete them too.

operator.description:
The identity provider the operator's staff sign in with to sign in as people of this app, for support. Defaults
to the one the platform passes in `PROTOBASE_OPERATOR_ISSUER`, `PROTOBASE_OPERATOR_CLIENT_ID` and
`PROTOBASE_OPERATOR_CLIENT_SECRET` (see `readOperatorSettings`), when set; `false` turns staff sign-in off
whatever the environment says.

signInProvider.description:
A sign-in provider the platform adds for people who already have an account: an OpenID Connect provider that never
signs anyone up. Defaults to the one the platform passes in `PROTOBASE_SIGN_IN_ISSUER`, `PROTOBASE_SIGN_IN_CLIENT_ID`
and `PROTOBASE_SIGN_IN_CLIENT_SECRET` (see `readPlatformSignIn`), when set; `false` turns it off whatever the
environment says. Left out when `socialProviders` has a provider with the same id.

sso.description:
Single sign-on with the app's SAML 2.0 identity providers, for example `{ saml: [{ id: 'okta', name: 'Okta',
domains: ['example.com'], idp: { metadata } }] }` (see `SamlProvider`). Like `socialProviders`, a provider signs up
people without an account, with the default role, but only at its `domains`, where it also links to the account
with the same address. Default none.

schema.description: The schema of the auth store in the app's database; default `auth`.

table.description: The table's name, default `user`, for example `users` for Supabase's `auth.users`.

columns.description:
The columns named otherwise than Protobase names them: `{ role: 'app_role' }`, where `role` holds something else
already, such as the Postgres role in Supabase's `auth.users`.

metadata.description: A JSON column that holds each user's metadata, such as `raw_user_meta_data`; none by default.

issuer.description: The provider's issuer URL; its settings are read from `{issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration`.

name.description: Shown on the staff sign-in page as "Continue with {name}". Default `the operator`.

group.description: The group in the ID token's `groups` claim that lets staff sign in as people. Default `protobase-staff-access`.

scopes.description: Scopes asked for besides `openid email profile`, for a provider that puts `groups` in the ID token only for one of its own.

acrValues.description: `acr` values that count as a strong sign-in, asked for as `acr_values`, for a provider that reports levels instead of `amr`.

sessionMinutes.description: How long a staff session lasts, in minutes: default 30, at most 240. It is not extended while in use.

issuer.description: The provider's issuer URL; its settings are read from `{issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration`.

provider.description:
The id of the provider: the button, the callback path, and the namespace of the linked accounts. Default `oidc`.
Use `github` only when the provider's `sub` is the GitHub user id, so its accounts are those of Better Auth's own
GitHub provider.

name.description: Shown on the sign-in page as "Continue with {name}". Default `GitHub` for the `github` provider, `SSO` otherwise.

scopes.description: Scopes asked for besides `openid email profile`.

id.description: The id: the button's `?sign-in=` link, the provider's paths and the namespace of its accounts. Lowercase letters, digits or "-".

name.description: Shown on the sign-in page as "Continue with {name}". Default `SSO`.

domains.description:
The email domains of its people, for example `['example.com']`; subdomains count. Only an address there signs up,
or links to the account that has it.

idp.description: The provider's metadata XML, or its entity ID, sign-in URL and signing certificate(s) (PEM; several while one rotates).

attributes.description: The assertion's attribute names, when they are not `email`, `givenName`, `surname` and `displayName`.

organizations.description: Whether the tokens carry organizations; read from `auth` when given. Needed with `jwksUrl` only.

jwksUrl.description: Or its JWKS endpoint, for an API that runs apart from the auth server. Needs `issuer`.

issuer.description: Defaults to the auth instance's `issuer`, its `baseURL`; it is both issuer and audience of its tokens.

cache.description: How long the key set is cached; see `cachedKeys`.

apps.description: Other Protobase apps whose users this API admits with their own tokens, so their admin apps can draw its resources (see `TrustedApp`).

audience.description: The audience the tokens must name; default `issuer`, the app's own tokens.

tenant.description: The one tenant everyone works in, for an app without organizations; never read from the token.

refreshMs.description: Reload the whole key set this often, so removed keys stop being accepted. Default 10 minutes.

minReloadMs.description: A token with an unknown `kid` reloads the set, but at most this often. Default 30 seconds.

maxAttempts.description: Tries before the job is kept as failed, listed in the admin app. Default 10.

retryDelay.description: The wait before the first retry, doubling with each one: milliseconds or text such as `30 seconds`. Default `2s`.

maxRetryDelay.description: The longest wait between two tries. Default `1 hour`.

timeout.description: How long one try may run before it counts as failed. Default `15 minutes`.

longQueries.description:
Its queries through `db` may run up to 30 seconds instead of the database's own limit, on a connection kept for
such work: for imports, backfills, large deletes and other bulk work.

concurrency.description: Jobs of this name running at once in each worker process. Default 1.

ordered.description:
Jobs run one at a time per group, in the order they were enqueued, and every enqueue names its group. A job that is
retrying or failed holds back the rest of its group until it succeeds, or is retried or deleted in the admin app.

schedule.description:
Runs the job on this cron schedule, such as `0 7 * * *` (with an optional seconds field first), with no payload: one
run per time, however many workers run. A run missed while no worker ran happens once, as soon as one does.

timezone.description: The time zone `schedule` is read in, such as `Europe/Amsterdam`. Default `UTC`.

description.description: What the job does, for the people who read the config and the failed jobs page.

arguments.description: Its arguments by name, each a field type or a type with options (see `ArgumentSpec`), such as `{ invoiceId: 'bigint' }`.

min.description: The least value, or for text the shortest length.

max.description: The greatest value, or for text the longest length.

scale.description: A decimal's number of digits after the point.

secret.description: Signs upload tickets and download URLs; default `PROTOBASE_FILES_SECRET`, then the app's `secret` (`PROTOBASE_SECRET`).

retention.description: How long bytes outlive their last reference, for restores; default `1 day`. Public providers default to 0.

trustedHosts.description:
Hosts whose images the admin app draws with the page's referrer, besides the app's own and those its providers link
public files from: `['images.example.com']`. Images from any other host load with `referrerPolicy="no-referrer"`.

storage.description:
Where `supabase.storage` keeps the bytes of its objects, which the app serves at `/api/sb/storage/v1` when it has an API key
(see `apiKeys`): `provider` names one of the providers, default `private`, and `maxFileSize` caps every upload, as
`50 MB` (the default) or a number of bytes; a bucket's own limit can only be lower. `false` serves no `/api/sb/storage/v1`.

providers.description:
Providers by name: `{ kind: 'local', dir }`, `{ kind: 's3', bucket }`, or `{ kind: 'custom' }`, the default export
of `files/<name>.ts`. Name the role (`archive`), not the vendor.

dir.description: The folder the files live in, created when missing; relative to the working directory.

public.description: Files anyone with the link may open, served without a signature.

publicUrl.description: Where public files are linked from instead of the app's own `/api/files/<provider>`, such as a CDN in front of it.

retention.description: How long bytes outlive their last reference; default `files.retention`, or 0 for a public provider.

prefix.description: The folder in the bucket that holds this provider's files, such as `acme/private`; default the bucket's root.

endpoint.description: The S3 API's address, such as `https://<account>.eu.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`; default AWS.

region.description: `auto` for R2, `fr-par` for Scaleway in Paris.

public.description: Files anyone with the link may open.

publicUrl.description: The bucket's public address, such as an R2 custom domain; public files are linked from there, under `prefix`.

retention.description: How long bytes outlive their last reference; default `files.retention`, or 0 for a public provider.

images.description: The image library of image fields' variants and placeholders, by its package name, loaded when the app serves.

schema.description:
The schema holding the outbox and the capture function, and the prefix of their transaction settings
(`changes.actor`, `changes.capture`); default `changes`. Rename it when the database already has a schema by that name.

days.description: Days a change is kept; a daily job deletes older ones. Kept forever when omitted.

processes.description:
`'one'`, the default, when one process serves the app: broadcasts and presence go between its channels in memory.
`'many'` when several processes serve it behind one address: they go between the processes through the
`realtime_relay` schema of the app's database, which `protobase migration` writes.

appId.description: The app's id on both iOS and Android, such as `com.example.shop`: two or more dot-separated parts, each a letter then letters and digits.

plugins.description: Extra native Capacitor plugins the app needs, as npm name → version range, such as `{ '@capacitor/camera': '^8.0.0' }`.

publicKey.description:
The public key, PEM, of the RSA key in `PROTOBASE_MOBILE_SIGNING_KEY`, which `protobase mobile keys`
prints: with it the Android and iOS app update themselves, taking only releases signed with that key.
